Upon loss of power via the upstream breaker, the unit did not generate a communication-loss alarm until approximately 20 minutes after the breaker was opened. This delay occurred because the HMI remained powered during that period. Once the HMI lost power, the unit fully shut down, generated the communication-loss alarm, and became inoperable.

Following power restoration, the unit did not operate in accordance with the Sequence of Operations. Unlike the other units tested, this unit did not drive the fans to 100% speed during the communication-loss condition. Instead, the fans modulated to approximately 500 RPM while communications remained unavailable.

critical.name: TST-581-12
critical.description: GLOBAL: Unit fails to adhere to SoO upon power failure. When local disconnects are opened, a comms loss is annunciated, whereupon the unit will shut down. When power is restored, the SoO states that fans shall be commanded to 100% operational speed for three minutes. This does not occur.

critical.name: TST-581-11
critical.description: GLOBAL: When placed in communications are severed from BMS, DH CRAH units continued to operate using the last known BMS setpoint rather than the locally configured setpoints. During testing, CTRL support changed the SAT SP through BMS to 60F, whereupon the CHW valve modulated open to 100% in an attempt to satisfy the new SAT SP. After the BMS CAT5/6 communication cable was disconnected, the CRAH maintained the 60F SAT SP rather than reverting to the local setpoints configured at the unit controller. This conflicts with the Mechanical SOO, which states: “In the event of a loss of communications, the CRAHs shall operate as stand-alone instances based on local set points from the design drawings and equipment schedules.”

critical.name: TST-581-8
critical.description: GLOBAL: Dirty filter alarm path appears correct only when testing through the exterior filter DP hose; however, the hose/test point will not hold pressure for manometer testing. Internal DP testing triggers a separate high-priority “Differential Pressure Sensor” alarm instead of the Dirty Filter Alarm. The "differential pressure sensor" BMS alarm is not listed in the CRAH points list within the controls bulletin but is listed in the submittal.
